item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1uc6a1 is 1uc6 chain A residues 6-109 from human ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, and d1o5dt2 is 1o5d chain T residues 107-205 from the extracellular region of human tissue factor. They are placed in the same Fibronectin type III family b.1.2.1, below the Fibronectin type III superfamily b.1.2, the immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold b.1, and the all-beta class b, so SCOPe treats their relationship as family-level homology, not merely same-fold resemblance. The fragment annotation on d1o5dt2 is a domain-level caveat: SCOPe flags it as 'fr', meaning that the entry is missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. That flag should not remove d1o5dt2 from b.1.2.1 or split it into a different family, but it should make any comparison coverage-aware. Align it only over the structurally present/core FnIII region, trim or mask unmatched columns when a full-domain alignment is required, and avoid interpreting gaps caused by the missing third as true insertions, deletions, or family-specific divergence. For representative selection, prefer a complete non-fragment b.1.2.1 domain such as d1uc6a1 when the set is meant to represent the common FnIII unit, and include d1o5dt2 only for tissue-factor-specific coverage or with a down-weight/exclusion rule in nonredundant training, template, and diversity panels. Otherwise the short coverage of d1o5dt2 can inflate apparent length and sequence diversity, bias consensus features, and provide a modeling template that cannot cover the missing common structure. Finally, family membership supports transfer of the broad FnIII beta-sandwich homology only; the fragment flag plus the different SCOPe protein nodes mean that cytokine-receptor-specific function from d1uc6a1 and tissue-factor/complex-specific function from d1o5dt2 should not be exchanged just because the fragments share b.1.2.1.","evidence_used":["get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/, /api/v1/releases/current","resolve_scop_identifier: /api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1uc6a1","resolve_scop_identifier: /api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1o5dt2","compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/homology, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/homology"]}]}
